pr_title: TransferEncoding chunked testing only if it is last header value
pr_body:
Fixes #63053

### Context
Transfer-Encodings are ordered and so the check should only succeed if "chunked" is the final Transfer-Encoding value
See #63053

### Changes made
Test only final value.
During `TransferEncodingChunked` is set to true, it is ensured `chunked` will be last value, even when it was already present.

### Testing
Few new unit tests.

### Note
This could be a **breaking change** if server behave out of spec. Currently if server send `Transfer-Encoding: chunked, gzip`, but actually do gzip and then chunk, client would have handled it without error, with changes in this PR it will fail to receive content.
pr_comments:
I believe this PR shall be abandoned. 
Reasoning: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/63053#issuecomment-2269303973

issue_context.title: SocketsHttpHandler does not check for Transfer-Encoding: chunked on response properly
issue_context.body:
For every HTTP/1.1 response, we need to check for Transfer-Encoding: chunked. We do this by calling HttpHeaders.ContainsParsedValue.

This check will succeed if "chunked" appears anywhere in the Transfer-Encoding list. However, Transfer-Encodings are ordered and so the check should only succeed if "chunked" is the final Transfer-Encoding value.

Note that sending "chunked" as a non-final Transfer-Encoding value is invalid server behavior, so we are only doing this incorrectly when the server is misbehaving. Still, we should adhere to the RFC here.

Relevant RFC: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7230.html#section-3.3.1

Issue Details
For every HTTP/1.1 response, we need to check for Transfer-Encoding: chunked. We do this by calling HttpHeaders.ContainsParsedValue. This check will succeed if "chunked" appears anywhere in the Transfer-Encoding list. However, Transfer-Encodings are ordered and so the check should only succeed if "chunked" is the final Transfer-Encoding value. Note that sending "chunked" as a non-final Transfer-Encoding value is invalid server behavior, so we are only doing this incorrectly when the server is misbehaving. Still, we should adhere to the RFC here. Relevant RFC: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7230.html#section-3.3.1
Author: geoffkizer
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Net.Http`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

Note this applies to both the public HttpResponseHeaders.TransferEncodingChunked property as well as our internal handling of Transfer-Encoding: chunked in HttpConnection (which uses the TransferEncodingChunked property today). We should ensure both are fixed.
Related: We should likely invert the order of checking `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` when both are present: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/62906#issuecomment-996078804
Note also, this applies to **setting** the HttpResponseHeaders.TransferEncodingChunked property as well. It should only remove "chunked" if it is the final Transfer-Encoding value.
Triage: Corner case, but still a bug.

> Related: We should likely invert the order of checking `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` when both are present: [#62906 (comment)](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/62906#issuecomment-996078804)

This has been already fixed

I was trying to understand risks of proposed solution in #105647 
In order to do that I have studied how common HTTP Client handle Transport-Encoding, created some simple local HTTP server and tested it. 
I have found that `Transport-Encoding` other than `chunked` is not implemented in any well used HTTP client. I have tested Chrome, Safari and curl and looked at source code of Kestrel and HttpClient.

I came to conclusion that current behavior of `HttpClient` is consistent with other major endpoint HTTP client implementations, i.e. if `chunked` appears in any order in `Transfer-Encoding` response is considered `chunked`.

For this reason I see any functional changes to current behavior as risky, same as chromium authors did in https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40620688

I therefore recommend to close this issue and linked PR as by-design.

@MihaZupan @karelz @ManickaP

I did some RFC reading and this part is interesting [[6.3.](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9112.html#rfc.section.6.3) [Message Body Length](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9112.html#message.body.length)](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9112.html#message.body.length) point 4.:
> If a [Transfer-Encoding](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9112.html#field.transfer-encoding) header field is present in a response and the chunked transfer coding is **not the final encoding**, the message body length is determined by reading the connection until it is closed by the server.

**BUT**, this was internally found and not reported by anyone, so I'm fine with keeping our behavior as-is.
I'm also fine with closing this. In case we have anyone reporting issue with the current behavior, we can always revisit this decision.

> I therefore recommend to close this issue and linked PR as by-design.

👍 as we've discussed, I agree changing this would be risky. Thanks for checking how other implementations behave here.
